title: Design patterns by intent
note: A design pattern is a named, reusable solution to a recurring design problem, not a piece of code to paste. The 1994 Gang of Four book catalogs 23 patterns in three groups: creational (how objects are made), structural (how objects are assembled), and behavioral (how objects share work and communicate).

read.title: Patterns are a shared vocabulary
text: In 1994 Erich Gamma, Richard Helm, Ralph Johnson, and John Vlissides, the Gang of Four, published 23 object-oriented design patterns. Their real gift was names. Saying "wrap it in an adapter" or "make the pricing rule a strategy" tells a teammate the structure you have in mind in a few words.

Several patterns look alike in code and differ only in intent, so learning the intent is the point. Adapter, Decorator, and Proxy all wrap another object. An adapter changes the interface so incompatible code can work together. A decorator keeps the interface and adds behavior, and decorators can be stacked. A proxy keeps the interface and controls access, for example by loading the real object lazily or checking permissions first. A facade is different again: it offers one simple interface over a whole subsystem.

Strategy and State are another lookalike pair. Both delegate work to a swappable object. With Strategy the client picks the algorithm, such as a sorting or pricing rule. With State the object switches its own behavior as its situation changes, such as a document moving from draft to published. Template Method solves a similar problem through inheritance rather than delegation, fixing the outline of an algorithm and letting subclasses fill in steps.
Patterns are tools, not goals. Forcing one where a plain function would do adds complexity without benefit.

o: A decorator converts to a new interface

q.q: In the State pattern, what triggers a change of behavior?
o: The client picks a new algorithm

q.q: How does Template Method differ from Strategy?
o: It uses inheritance rather than delegation
It creates objects instead of running algorithms
